New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani marked Rakshabandhan by joining celebrations with South Asian seniors at India Home, a senior care home in the city. Extending his wishes to the community, Mamdani also shared wholesome images of the celebration on X, showing him interacting with women as they tied rakhis on his wrist.Mamdani used the festival to highlight its message of protection, support and solidarity, while drawing a broader connection between the traditional bond represented by the rakhi and his relationship with New Yorkers.“On Raksha Bandhan, a single thread symbolises a powerful promise: to protect, support, and stand by one another,” Mamdani said.Traditionally, Rakshabandhan celebrates the bond between brothers and sisters, with the sister tying a rakhi around her brother’s wrist as a symbol of affection and a promise of protection. Mamdani sought to extend that symbolism beyond the traditional relationship, presenting the thread as a reminder of the trust, responsibility and mutual support that can bind a community together.The mayor said he was glad to share the occasion with elders at India Home, which provides South Asian seniors with a space for community, care and companionship. He described the sense of belonging offered by the organisation as an example of the importance of building strong community ties.“Today I shared in the joy of this ceremony with elders at India Home, where South Asian seniors find community, care, and chosen family,” he wrote.Mamdani then linked the spirit of Rakshabandhan to his broader vision for New York City, calling on residents to extend the values of care and solidarity beyond the festival.“That spirit extends to our entire city. May we continue to stand by one another as we build a safer and more affordable city for all,” he said.His Rakshabandhan message comes as Mamdani continues to emphasise community, affordability and safety as key themes of his political agenda in New York. By sharing the festival with members of the city’s South Asian senior community, he also highlighted the cultural diversity and community networks that form part of New York’s social fabric.
Article Summary: Zohran Mamdani marked Rakshabandhan by joining celebrations with South Asian seniors at India Home, a senior care home in the city. He used the festival to highlight its message of protection, support and solidarity, while drawing a connection between the traditional bond represented by the rakhi and his relationship with New Yorkers.

Article Title: No escape for Trump in hush money case as US judge blocks bid to shift federal court
Article Text:
US President Donald Trump

Judge rejects Trump’s immunity argument

Trump to appeal latest setback

US President Donald Trump ’s bid to wipe out his New York hush money conviction has hit another roadblock, with a federal judge ruling that the case cannot be moved from state to federal court. Manhattan-based US district judge Alvin Hellerstein on Friday rejected Trump’s latest attempt to shift the case, saying the conduct involved was personal and not part of his official duties as president.The ruling came after a three-judge panel of the 2nd US Circuit Court of Appeals asked Hellerstein to take a closer look at how a July 2024 Supreme Court ruling on presidential immunity applied to Trump’s case.At the centre of the dispute is Trump’s conviction over a $130,000 payment made to porn star Stormy Daniels . Trump was found guilty in May 2024 on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records in a case brought by Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg.Daniels had claimed she had a sexual encounter with Trump, which could have affected his 2016 presidential campaign. Trump has denied the claim and has said the case was politically motivated.Trump’s lawyers argued that the Supreme Court’s July 2024 ruling should help overturn his conviction. In Trump v. United States, the Supreme Court ruled that presidents have immunity from prosecution for official acts. It also said prosecutors cannot use evidence of official acts in criminal cases involving private conduct.Trump argued that the ruling applied to his case because jurors heard evidence from his first term in the White House, including testimony from former White House communications director Hope Hicks.Hellerstein, however, said the case was about Trump’s personal conduct rather than his presidential actions."Paying hush money to an adult film star or engaging in a cover-up of an embarrassment are not subsumed in presidential immunity," Hellerstein wrote.Hellerstein, who was appointed by former Democratic president Bill Clinton, had already rejected Trump’s attempt to move the case to federal court twice. The appeals court later asked him to examine whether the evidence in question "relates to acts taken under color of the Presidency."Trump has also asked a New York state appeals court to throw out his conviction. His lawyers notified the court on Friday that they would appeal Hellerstein’s decision."President Trump will be ‌filing a ⁠powerful appeal, and will continue defeating Democrat weaponization at every turn," a spokesman for Trump’s legal team said in a statement cited by Reuters.Trump did not receive jail time or a fine for the conviction. On January 10, 2025, trial judge Juan Merchan sentenced him to an unconditional discharge, leaving the conviction in place.Merchan said the punishment would avoid disrupting Trump’s second term as president, which began on January 20, 2025.Trump faced four criminal cases and denied wrongdoing in all of them. The case brought by Bragg was the only one that went to trial.The three judges on the appeals court were appointed by Democratic presidents, while Bragg is also a Democrat.
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump's bid to wipe out his New York hush money conviction has hit another roadblock. A federal judge has ruled that the case cannot be moved from state to federal court. Trump was found guilty in May 2024 on 34 felony counts of falsifying business records in a case brought by Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg.

Article Title: US to establish first space academy, expand 'far beyond the Moon'
Article Text:
The proposed ‘US Space Academy’ intends to strengthen the nation’s space workforce and develop the next generation of space leaders (Photo: Nasa).

US President Donald Trump signed an executive order on Friday to establish the country’s first space academy and interacted with astronauts stationed at the International Space Station, during a visit to Nasa ’s Mission Control in Houston.According to a Nasa press release, the proposed ‘US Space Academy’ intends to strengthen the nation’s space workforce and develop the next generation of space leaders.“Given the rapid growth of the US Space Force and commercial space industry, and the expansion of our ambitions to the Moon and far beyond the Moon, it’s clear we will need to educate and train an entire generation of skilled service members, engineers, and civil operators”, Trump said.Nasa administrator Jared Isaacman has been appointed as the chair of a new Presidential Commission on the United States Space Academy, while Nasa deputy administrator Matt Anderson will serve as the executive director.“In the years ahead, we will return Nasa astronauts to the lunar surface, build the Moon Base, get underway on nuclear power, ignite the orbital economy and launch more missions of science and discovery,” said Isaacman.On August 20, Trump signed the National Space Transportation Policy, a framework to guide safe, reliable, and affordable access to space for civil, commercial, and national security missions.In December 2025, Trump had also signed the Ensuring American Space Superiority, aiming to send American astronauts back to the Moon by 2028, build a permanent base on the Moon by 2030, and replace the old International Space Station with a commercial version by 2030.Trump also presented the Congressional Space Medal of Honour to the Artemis II mission crew, which travelled around the Moon in April and recorded the biggest distance from Earth for a manned space mission.Trump also interacted with the Nasa astronauts Jack Hathaway, Anil Menon, and Jessica Meir, who are part of Expedition 75 to the International Space Station.
Article Summary: The proposed ‘US Space Academy’ intends to strengthen the nation’s space workforce and develop the next generation of space leaders. Trump also interacted with astronauts stationed at the International Space Station, during a visit to Nasa ’s Mission Control in Houston.

Article Title: 'I still struggle': Landlady recalls Saudi man who brought 9/11 hijackers to her office
Article Text:
Landlady recalls Saudi facilitator who brought 9/11 hijackers to her

Holly Ratchford, who managed a residential complex in California's San Diego where two of the 9/11 hijackers lived, has spoken publicly for the first time about her encounters with Saudi national Omar al-Bayoumi, who is accused of helping the two men before the attacks.Speaking to the BBC, Ratchford said she still struggles to reconcile the friendly man she knew with the allegations surrounding him. “It's almost impossible for me to wrap my head around who he said he was, and who he really is. I still struggle with that,” she said.Bayoumi moved with his family into Parkwood Apartments in September 1999 and soon became a regular at Ratchford's pool parties. She described him as “always so bubbly and smiling” and “very, very friendly”.In February 2000, Bayoumi brought two men, Nawaf al-Hazmi and Khalid al-Mihdhar, to Ratchford's office seeking an apartment. The pair did not meet the complex's income requirements, but Bayoumi co-signed their lease and helped them open a bank account.Hazmi and Mihdhar later became two of the 19 al-Qaeda members who hijacked four US passenger planes on September 11, 2001.The two were on American Airlines Flight 77, which crashed into the Pentagon.Ratchford said she had no reason at the time to suspect the men. “There was absolutely nothing unusual about them. They were nice, they were polite,” she told the BBC.She later learned of their identities in the aftermath of the attacks, when a woman who claimed to be seeking a rental reference asked her whether she knew they were terrorists who had flown a plane into the Pentagon.“And I went, ‘What?’” Ratchford recalled.The FBI interviewed her on September 14, 2001, and obtained Bayoumi's guarantor form. Former FBI investigator Richard Lambert told the BBC that investigators later identified “a network headed up by Omar al-Bayoumi”.Bayoumi has long faced allegations that he facilitated the hijackers' activities in San Diego.In an August 2025 ruling, a New York federal judge found that evidence created a “reasonable inference” that Bayoumi and a Saudi diplomat had been coordinating with the Saudi government while assisting the hijackers. Saudi Arabia and Bayoumi have denied the allegations and Saudi Arabia is appealing the ruling.Ratchford, who has provided a sealed declaration to the New York court, said she has been haunted by her connection to the three men for the past 25 years.
Article Summary: Omar al-Bayoumi is accused of helping two of the 9/11 hijackers before the attacks. Landlady Holly Ratchford said she still struggles to reconcile the friendly man she knew with the allegations surrounding him. Bayoumi moved with his family into Parkwood Apartments in September 1999 and soon became a regular at RATCHford's pool parties.

Article Title: Chinese hackers did not target Nasa, Senate - US reverses statement on agency breaches
Article Text:
An FBI investigation found that an attempted intrusion into NASA was unsuccessful after the agency patched the software targeted by the hackers.

FBI affidavit reveals scope of hacking campaign

US seizes hacking infrastructure

US authorities have corrected earlier claims that several major government agencies had been hacked by a Chinese state-sponsored cyber group, clarifying that some were targeted but not necessarily compromised.The US Department of Justice said on Friday that the Senate, Federal Reserve, NASA and several other agencies were “among the targets” of QTFY, a China-linked hacking group accused of conducting a years-long cyber-espionage campaign.The correction narrows the scope of the breaches confirmed by US authorities. The DOJ said an earlier statement released on August 26 had incorrectly described all the agencies as victims, while an FBI affidavit showed that they had all been targeted but only some were successfully compromised.According to the FBI affidavit, QTFY has targeted US federal networks since at least 2018, including those belonging to Nasa, the Federal Reserve, the Department of Energy, the Justice Department, the Department of Health and Human Services, the National Institutes of Health and the US Senate.The affidavit also provides details about the outcomes of some of the attacks.An FBI investigation found that an attempted intrusion into NASA was unsuccessful after the agency patched the software targeted by the hackers.However, US authorities said the group successfully carried out intrusions in September 2024 at three Department of Energy national laboratories, an NIH facility, an HHS agency and a US security-device manufacturer.A joint advisory from the FBI, National Security Agency and US Cyber Command also said hackers had successfully stolen data from unnamed defence contractors, financial institutions and universities in May 2024. Attempts to access the networks of the US Senate and a US hospital in March 2026 were unsuccessful.The clarification came as US authorities announced the seizure of two internet domains allegedly linked to QTFY's hacking infrastructure, known as QScan and QTRouter.The DOJ alleged that the platforms were operated by a China-based company and used to scan and infect internet-connected devices, creating a network that could route malicious traffic through compromised systems around the world. This allegedly helped hackers conceal the true origin of attacks.FBI Director Kash Patel said the tools were used by Chinese cyber actors to hide the source of attacks targeting US critical infrastructure.The DOJ said the seized domains were embedded in the malware and were required for communication and authentication, making QScan and QTRouter inoperable after the court-authorised seizures.China's embassy in Washington rejected the US allegations, accusing Washington of using cybersecurity claims to “smear or discredit China”.
Article Summary: US authorities have corrected earlier claims that several major government agencies had been hacked by a Chinese state-sponsored cyber group. The US Department of Justice said on Friday that the Senate, Federal Reserve, NASA and several other agencies were ‘among the targets’ of QTFY, a China-linked hacking group.

Article Title: Built for $70,000 in 1976, this underground Missouri concrete home survived a deadly F4 tornado; 50 years later, it remains almost invisible from the road, hidden beneath a hillside
Article Text:
This Missouri home looks like a hillside from the outside, but beneath the earth is a remarkably engineered residence.

A house hidden inside the hillside

Covered with earth and vegetation, the home's roof doubles as a natural landscape where turtles, birds and groundhogs roam.

Built with concrete and post-tensioned beams

The home was built for $70,000

The 1990 tornado that tested the underground house

Built with post-tensioned concrete and engineered to support 250 pounds per square foot, the structure was designed for exceptional strength and durability.

‘The house did its work as a shelter’

An underground house that doesn't feel underground

Large glass walls and skylights flood the underground home with natural light, challenging the idea that underground houses are dark and gloomy.

The earth helps regulate the temperature

The home's concrete walls and surrounding earth provide thermal mass, helping maintain a more stable indoor temperature throughout the year.

A roof that becomes part of the landscape

The north-facing home uses the earth itself as part of its environmental strategy, reducing the impact of extreme outdoor temperatures.

Nearly 50 years later, the experiment still works

When Tim and Monica open the front door of their home in Springfield, Missouri, there is little to suggest that a house is hidden beneath the hillside outside. Only a small corner of the structure is visible from the road, while much of the home disappears into the earth.The unusual underground residence was recently featured by architecture and design-focused YouTube channel Kirsten Dirksen, offering a look inside a home that was designed nearly five decades ago around the idea of becoming part of the landscape rather than sitting on top of it.Built in 1976 by architect and builder Dennis Spencer, the house occupies a sloping, north-facing site in Springfield. Instead of treating the difficult orientation and hillside as obstacles, Spencer incorporated them into the design, creating a concrete structure that is largely buried beneath earth and vegetation.For Tim and Monica, the unusual design has become an everyday reality. From the outside, even delivery drivers can struggle to identify the property as a house."There’s not a lot of concrete underground houses," they explain in the Kirsten Dirksen video, noting that the home is particularly unusual for Springfield.The property was designed to blend into its surroundings. The roof is covered with roughly 14 to 15 inches of earth and vegetation, allowing grass and other natural elements to grow above the structure.Wildlife has seemingly accepted the house as part of the hillside. Turtles can be seen on the roof, birds inhabit the surrounding trees and a family of groundhogs has even made its home in the owners’ burn pile."The animals barely see the house. They think of it as kind of part of the hill," one of the homeowners says in the video.That was precisely the point of Spencer’s design.The house does not announce itself from the road. Instead, it nestles into the land, with only limited portions visible from outside. The result is a structure that appears less like a conventional residence and more like an extension of the hillside.Despite its seemingly natural appearance, the house is an extensively engineered concrete structure.It was constructed with cast-in-place concrete and post-tensioning technology. The roof uses a seven-inch concrete slab supported by upturned beams and was engineered to carry about 250 pounds per square foot.The construction technique involved allowing the concrete to cure before tensioning cables were installed. The cables compress the concrete, increasing its strength and durability.There are only three columns within the main interior space, allowing much of the home's interior to remain open and flexible.The roof was particularly important because it had to support the earth that would eventually be placed over the structure.The earth covering is not simply decorative. It forms part of the home's environmental strategy, helping insulate the interior and moderate temperatures throughout the year.The unusual project was also remarkably inexpensive by today's standards.Spencer initially obtained a $50,000 loan to construct the house and later secured another $20,000, bringing the total cost to around $70,000.Securing financing was reportedly difficult because banks were unfamiliar with such an unconventional design."You present a set of plans for something so unique, the banks have a little hard time with it," the homeowners explain.Despite the challenges, Spencer completed the home and created a structure that would ultimately prove its worth in one of the most dangerous weather events to hit the neighbourhood.Springfield lies in an area vulnerable to severe tornadoes, making the home's ability to withstand extreme weather a significant part of its story.In November 1990, an F4 tornado tore through the subdivision, destroying or severely damaging neighbouring properties and bringing down 41 mature trees around the underground house.The tornado passed directly over the property.While nearby conventional homes suffered devastating damage, the underground structure largely remained intact.The homeowners recall that the aftermath was more of a cleanup operation than a major repair project. The cars were destroyed, trees came down across the property and neighbouring houses were badly damaged, but the earth-covered concrete structure continued to provide shelter.The home's performance during the tornado demonstrated one of the fundamental principles behind its design: the earth itself could become a form of protection.For Spencer, the home's relationship with the landscape was not simply an aesthetic decision. Its position within the hillside also gave it an inherent advantage during severe weather.One of the home's lowest and most deeply buried areas provided a particularly protected space during the tornado."You really do feel the sense of comfort, this safety, feeling like you're coming into the land but still having the shelter," the homeowners say.The house's concrete structure, combined with the earth berm surrounding it, effectively separated the living spaces from much of the destructive force experienced above ground.The tornado also provided an unintended real-world test of Spencer's approach to resilient architecture.Despite being surrounded by earth, the interior is far removed from the dark, enclosed image often associated with underground homes.Tim recalls growing up exploring caves in Missouri and describes them as fascinating but sometimes dark and unsettling. This house, however, was designed to avoid that feeling.Natural light enters through skylights and large areas of glass. A ten-foot wall of east-facing glass helps connect the main living spaces to the landscape, while the layout creates repeated visual connections between the interior and exterior.The home includes a kitchen, dining area and living spaces with ceilings reaching around 10 feet in some areas.As the occupants move through the house, ceiling heights and corridors change, creating what the designers describe as moments of "compression and expansion." Narrower passages lead into larger rooms and courtyards, giving the interior a changing sense of scale.Even some of the deepest rooms remain visually connected to the outside through carefully positioned openings.The home's underground location also contributes to its energy efficiency.Concrete has significant thermal mass, allowing it to absorb heat and release it gradually as surrounding temperatures change. Combined with the earth surrounding the structure, this creates a stable indoor environment.The home's design takes advantage of this thermal inertia to reduce the impact of extreme outdoor temperatures.Although the property has modern mechanical systems, its occupants say the structure could remain comfortable even with those systems switched off under suitable conditions, relying on its relationship with the earth, ventilation and natural protection.The north-facing site presented a challenge for passive solar design because it limits exposure to the strongest southern winter sun. Spencer instead used the earth as a major component of the home's environmental strategy.Perhaps the most striking feature is that the roof does not look like a conventional roof at all.With earth and vegetation covering the concrete structure, the roof becomes an extension of the hillside.In winter, the design takes on another role. Snow-covered slopes can make the home appear even more deeply embedded in the landscape, while the shape of the roof has also tempted neighbourhood children to use it for sledding."The land's just wrapping its arms around you," one of the homeowners says, describing the feeling of living beneath the hillside.The house's relationship with nature extends beyond its thermal performance. Wildlife treats the property as part of its habitat rather than as a conventional human structure.Spencer's decision to build underground in 1976 may have seemed radical at the time, but nearly five decades later the house continues to demonstrate the potential of architecture that responds directly to its environment.It is difficult to spot from the street, difficult for delivery drivers to locate and almost indistinguishable from the surrounding landscape.But beneath the grass and earth is a carefully engineered concrete structure designed for strength, energy efficiency and resilience.Its survival of a devastating F4 tornado remains perhaps the clearest demonstration of the concept.While conventional houses around it were exposed to the full force of the storm, Spencer's home was protected by the very landscape into which he had built it.
Article Summary: The home in Springfield, Missouri, was built in 1976 by architect and builder Dennis Spencer. It was designed to blend into its surroundings, with only limited portions visible from the road. The roof is covered with roughly 14 to 15 inches of earth and vegetation, allowing grass and other natural elements to grow above the structure.

Article Title: Pakistan: Three missing men found dead with alleged torture marks in Balochistan
Article Text:
Representative file photo (IANS photo)

Three bodies recovered in Balochistan's Usta Muhammad have reportedly been identified as men who had earlier gone missing, with local sources alleging that they were forcibly disappeared after being detained by Pakistani security forces.According to The Balochistan Post, the deceased have been identified as Hafiz Mohammad Waqas, a Levies personnel from Machh in Bolan, his brother Mittha Khan, son of Nawab Khan, and Maqbool Ahmed, son of Jan Mohammad, a resident of Dasht Sabzband.Waqas was reportedly taken into custody and forcibly disappeared in May 2026. The three bodies were recovered from Usta Muhammad on August 24, according to local sources cited by the publication.The sources said the bodies bore apparent signs of torture. However, the circumstances surrounding their deaths have not been independently established, and no official findings from an investigation have been made public.The recoveries come amid reports of more than 15 bodies being found in different parts of Balochistan in recent days, including Panjgur, Mastung and Kharan. Several bodies recovered from Panjgur were allegedly identified as people who had previously been reported missing, while the identities of others remain unknown.The latest cases have renewed scrutiny of allegations of enforced disappearances in Balochistan, where rights groups and political organisations have for years raised concerns over the fate of missing people.Baloch political and human rights organisations have accused Pakistani security institutions of detaining people and, in some cases, killing them in custody before abandoning their bodies. Pakistan's authorities and security institutions have repeatedly denied involvement in enforced disappearances and allegations of extrajudicial killings.Rights groups and political organisations have called for credible and transparent investigations into the reported disappearances and deaths. They have also demanded that missing individuals be produced before courts, their families be informed of their whereabouts, and anyone accused of wrongdoing be subjected to due legal process.
Article Summary: Three bodies recovered in Balochistan's Usta Muhammad have reportedly been identified as men who had earlier gone missing. Local sources allege they were forcibly disappeared after being detained by Pakistani security forces. The circumstances surrounding their deaths have not been independently established, and no official findings from an investigation have been made public.

Article Title: 15 newborns killed in fire at Islamabad hospital's gynaecology ward in Pakistan
Article Text:
The fire reportedly started after an air-conditioner compressor exploded inside the nursery, according to rescue sources.

Poll Vote & Share your view What should hospitals prioritise to prevent fire-related tragedies? Stronger fire-safety measures Regular safety inspections 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

15 newborns died after a fire broke out in the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad on Wednesday.According to PIMS officials, the nursery housed 16 newborns when the fire broke out, with only one baby rescued from the ward, reported local outlet Geo News. The fire reportedly started after an air-conditioner compressor exploded inside the nursery, according to rescue officials.The blaze broke out at around 7 am in the gynaecology ward of the hospital on the third floor of the MCH ward, in Pakistan's federal capital. Rescue teams were deployed to the hospital and worked to extinguish the fire and evacuate those inside while carrying out cooling operations at the site.According to the district administration, 14 of the 15 children killed were completely burnt.The incident has raised concerns over safety measures in the hospital's neonatal and maternity facilities.Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has ordered an immediate investigation into the incident and directed authorities to identify those responsible and take strict action. He expressed deep grief over the deaths, saying that a tragedy involving children was an “irreparable loss”, and said he shared the grief of the bereaved parents.The Prime Minister also directed authorities to conduct a detailed review of fire-safety arrangements and the factors that contributed to the incident, with the aim of preventing similar tragedies in hospitals.Meanwhile, an inquiry committee headed by the additional deputy commissioner general has also been formed to determine how the fire started and establish responsibility. The blaze broke out in the hospital’s gynaecology ward, where the nursery was located.
Article Summary: 15 newborns died after a fire broke out in the gynaecology ward of the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences in Islamabad. The fire reportedly started after an air-conditioner compressor exploded inside the nursery, according to rescue sources. Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif has ordered an immediate investigation into the incident.

Article Title: Five labourers gunned down at construction site in Pakistan's Balochistan
Article Text: Five labourers from Pakistan’s Punjab province were shot dead at a construction site in Balochistan’s Pishin district, a provincial government official said Tuesday, according to news agency PTI.The labourers were killed by unidentified gunmen in Saranan town on Monday morning, Balochistan government spokesperson Shahid Rind said. Their bodies were sent to their hometowns in Punjab for burial.Arrangements were made to transport the bodies to their respective villages in Ahmedpur Sharqia and Bahawalpur, Rind said. Security forces have launched a search operation to track down the attackers.Balochistan chief minister Sarfaraz Bugti condemned the killings and vowed action against those responsible."Those shedding the blood of innocent laborers deserve no leniency," Bugti said in a statement issued by his office. "The cowardly acts of terrorists cannot weaken the provincial government's resolve."Saranan town has witnessed militant attacks since last week. A few days ago, gunmen attacked a police station in the town and fled with weapons, ammunition and two vehicles.Banned Baloch insurgent groups have frequently targeted workers and labourers from other provinces working in Balochistan.In July, five barbers from Multan were shot dead in Mashkail town after armed men on motorcycles opened fire at their barber shop.Last month, six labourers from Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa were abducted in the Nasirabad area of Turbat district. Their bullet-riddled bodies were later found in a remote area, police said.Security and law enforcement agencies have been conducting a large-scale operation against insurgent groups in parts of Balochistan since early July. However, the attacks have continued.In a separate incident on Sunday, five policemen were injured when two unidentified men hurled a hand grenade at a police post in Ambar tehsil of Mohmand district in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.Police retaliated with gunfire, forcing the attackers to flee. The injured policemen were taken to a nearby hospital and are said to be out of danger. An investigation is underway.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which borders Afghanistan, has witnessed recurring militant violence, including attacks linked to insurgent groups, cross-border movement of fighters and repeated military operations.
Article Summary: The labourers were killed by unidentified gunmen in Saranan town on Monday morning. Security forces have launched a search operation to track down the attackers. Baloch insurgent groups have frequently targeted workers and labourers from other provinces working in Balochistan. In July, five barbers from Multan were shot dead in Mashkail town.

Article Title: Pakistan army officer pulls gun, fires in air amid student protest at Peshawar university- video
Article Text:
Sarhad University, Peshawar, Pakistan (Picture from X)

A Pakistan army officer opened fire into the air during a student protest at Sarhad University in Peshawar, triggering chaos and a scuffle on the campus, according to local media reports and videos circulating online.The incident comes amid growing unrest in Pakistan, with protests and demonstrations also being reported from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and Balochistan, adding to the challenges facing the country's military and political establishment.According to reports, the officer, said to be a colonel, was the husband of a faculty member at Sarhad University. He reportedly got into a heated confrontation with protesting students, which soon escalated into a physical scuffle.Videos shared by several social media accounts purportedly show the officer striking students with a stick amid the confrontation. As tensions escalated, he allegedly pulled out a pistol and initially pointed it towards the protesters before raising the weapon in the air.The officer was then seen firing shots into the air, sparking panic and further uproar on the university campus.Reports said the officer has been taken into custody, while the Pakistan army has ordered an inquiry into the incident.
Article Summary: Pakistan army officer opened fire during student protest at Sarhad University. Incident triggered chaos and a scuffle on the campus, according to reports. Incident comes amid growing unrest in Pakistan, with protests and demonstrations also being reported from Pakistan-occupied Kashmir and Balochistan.

Article Title: ‘CTA intentionally prevented’: PTI alleges negligence over Imran Khan’s hospital visit
Article Text:
Imran Khan’s medical care under scrutiny

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you think the inquiry committee established by Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif will lead to accountability? Yes, it will No, it won't 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), the party of former Prime Minister Imran Khan, on Monday criticised what it called the “continued failure” of authorities at a state-run hospital, alleging that a CT Coronary Angiography (CTA) scheduled for Khan was not conducted despite cardiologists warning of potential cardiac complications.In a statement on Sunday, PTI central secretary Information Sheikh Waqas Akram said authorities had failed to provide the 73-year-old Khan with the medically recommended diagnostic test despite a functional CT scanner being available at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS), Dawn reported."This cannot be dismissed as an isolated administrative lapse; it reflects a deeply troubling pattern,” Akram said.Akram also cited a Supreme Court order directing Khan to undergo a comprehensive medical examination and treatment at Shifa International Hospital.He alleged that authorities had bypassed the directive and instead transferred Khan to a facility where the CT angiography was not conducted.“When the necessary facilities were available at Shifa International, deliberately taking Khan to a hospital unable or unwilling to perform the procedure raises a grave question: was the decision made in advance to prevent the CT Coronary Angiography from being conducted?” he asked."Even the government’s own doctors considered this diagnostic test necessary,” Akram added.Akram said a government medical board examined Khan on August 10 after he complained of heart palpitations and severe headaches.He said a cardiologist at PIMS had recommended a CTA on August 1 after Khan experienced fluctuating blood pressure and restlessness, citing potential cardiac complications given his age and prolonged isolation.Taking note of the reports, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday formed an inquiry committee, headed by the Establishment Division secretary, to establish the facts and determine responsibility.Commenting on the Prime Minister’s decision to constitute an inquiry committee following reports that Imran Khan’s CTA was not conducted, Akram said the move raised “serious questions as to why the medically recommended test was not conducted in the first instance. Why coordination between the cardiology and radiology departments had failed, and why Imran Khan was not taken to Shifa International despite the availability of the required facilities there”."Imran Khan’s heart health cannot be subjected to political calculations, administrative excuses or further delay,” Akram said."Political victimisation must never be permitted to endanger a human life through the denial or postponement of essential medical care. The decision to take him to a facility where the required test was not conducted, despite the availability of the necessary facilities at Shifa International, has created serious concerns that the procedure was intentionally prevented,” he alleged."The government and all relevant authorities will bear full responsibility for any further deterioration in his condition,” Akram added.Meanwhile, former India captains Sunil Gavaskar, Kapil Dev and Dilip Vengsarkar are among 21 former international cricket captains who have written to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, urging authorities to ensure proper medical treatment and the welfare of Imran Khan.The letter, initiated by former Australia captain Greg Chappell, marks the second appeal by former international cricketers calling for humane treatment and adequate medical care for the 73-year-old Khan.Khan was arrested on August 5, 2023, in connection with a corruption case and has remained in custody since then. He is currently lodged in Adiala Jail, a detention facility on the outskirts of Rawalpindi.Khan’s relatives and supporters have repeatedly alleged human rights violations and accused authorities of restricting his access to adequate medical care, family visits and legal counsel.
Article Summary: Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI), the party of former Prime Minister Imran Khan, on Monday criticised what it called the “continued failure” of authorities at a state-run hospital. PTI alleges that a CT Coronary Angiography (CTA) scheduled for Khan was not conducted despite cardiologists warning of potential cardiac complications. Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Saturday formed an inquiry committee, headed by the Establishment Division secretary.

Article Title: ‘You are powerful, but remember 1971?’ Pakistani politician takes fresh swipe at Army
Article Text:
Fazlur Rehman (File photo)

(With ANI inputs)

Pakistani politician and Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman continued his verbal attacks on the Pakistan Army, recalling the military's decisive defeat in the 1971 war with India that led to the creation of Bangladesh, then known as East Pakistan.“‘We are the protectors of this country. No one’s father can harm this country.’ I agree, you are very powerful,” Rehman remarked at a JUI (F) convention in Peshawar, targeting Pakistan’s top military leadership.He recalled how the Pakistan Army laid down its arms in 1971, just a day after then-President and military ruler General Yahya Khan declared that it would fight until the end."But I remember, and maybe there are some elders who remember, that in December 1971, one day before laying down arms, General Yahya Khan addressed the army and said, we will fight in the streets, in the deserts, in the fields, in the factories, in the mountains, and we will fight against them. We will fight. We heard these big words then," Rehman added.The JUI-F further chief questioned why the public is being subjected to "severe hardships" while the establishment remains "insensitive" to their misery.“Why are you putting the country and the people to the test? Why are you having fun when your public is suffering? And today is 2026. When the revolution came in Afghanistan in 1989, and the war started, now you tell me, it’s been 45-46 years, blood has been flowing on the same line for about half a century.When blood flows like this, then it is a sign of geographical changes,” Rehman remarked.Warning that persistent state oppression and ongoing conflict threaten the nation’s integrity and could signal territorial disintegration, he stated, “It is a sign of oppression. Then at least inform us of your intentions. We are tolerating it and will continue to tolerate it. It will continue. A few more days, my dear, just a few more days. We are forced to take a breath in the shade of oppression. If we endure the oppression for a little longer, if we suffer, if we cry, it is the legacy of our ancestors. We are helpless.”Rehman’s remarks came days after he challenged the military to enter politics directly, declaring, “If you want to do politics, then take off the uniform and come; participate in the elections, and it will become clear what votes people give to those in uniform. It is your prerogative to give government to whomever you want, and to snatch it away from whomever you wish.”
Article Summary: Jamiat Ulema-e-Islam (F) chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman continued his verbal attacks on the Pakistan Army. He recalled the military's decisive defeat in the 1971 war with India that led to the creation of Bangladesh. He questioned why the public is being subjected to "severe hardships" while the establishment remains "insensitive"

Article Title: Pakistan: Security official killed by unidentified gunmen; 5 cops injured in separate grenade blast
Article Text:
According to police, two unidentified armed men targeted the security official. (Photo credit: IANS)

Five policemen injured in grenade attack

A security official was killed on Sunday after unidentified gunmen opened fire in northwest Pakistan, police said, according to news agency PTI.The incident took place within the jurisdiction of Badaber Police Station on the outskirts of Peshawar, the capital of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.According to police, two unidentified armed men riding a motorcycle targeted the official, who was posted with the Counter Terrorism Department.He was killed on the spot, while the assailants fled the scene following the attack. Police cordoned off the area and launched a search operation to trace the attackers.No individual or group has so far claimed responsibility for the attack.In a separate incident in Mohmand district, five policemen were injured when two unidentified men hurled a hand grenade at a police post in Ambar tehsil, police said.Police retaliated with gunfire, forcing the attackers to flee. The injured policemen were taken to a nearby hospital and are said to be out of danger. An investigation is underway.Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, which borders Afghanistan, has witnessed recurring militant violence, cross-border movement of fighters and military operations.Pakistan's federal government has blamed the banned Tehreek-e-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) for attacks in areas bordering Afghanistan since a ceasefire agreement between the two sides ended in November 2022.
Article Summary: A security official was killed on Sunday after unidentified gunmen opened fire in northwest Pakistan. In a separate incident, five policemen were injured when two unidentified men hurled a hand grenade at a police post in Ambar tehsil. The injured policemen were taken to a nearby hospital and are said to be out of danger.

Article Title: Pakistan power crisis: Karachi residents riot amid outages lasting hours, block major roads
Article Text:
Protesters blocked major roads and intersections, burned tyres and clashed with K-Electric personnel over prolonged blackouts (ANI photo)

Power protests erupted across several parts of Karachi as residents took to the streets over prolonged and unannounced outages, blocking major roads and burning tyres while demanding restoration of electricity.Demonstrations were reported in Pak Colony, Liaquatabad, Gharibabad, Nishtar Road, Bhimpura and Ranchore Line, disrupting traffic across key parts of Pakistan’s commercial capital. In Liaquatabad, protesters blocked major intersections, while clashes between traders and K-Electric (KE) staff over outages escalated into tyre-burning on Nishtar Road, as reported by local news outle Dawn.Residents said they were facing 12 hours or more of daily power cuts, often without adequate notice. The outages have also disrupted water supplies as pumping stations remain shut when electricity is unavailable, adding to public anger.“Bill-paying citizens are being punished with 12-hour load-shedding,” a protester in Liaquatabad said.The crisis also hit businesses and households, with residents reporting spoiled food, disrupted studies and sleepless nights as fans remained unusable during blackouts.The protests compounded an already severe traffic situation in the city. Roads were also closed for traditional Chup Tazia processions, while the power protests triggered additional blockades. Traffic police diverted vehicles to alternative routes, but those too became congested.Asif Khan, a private-sector employee, told Dawn he took four hours to travel from SITE to Liaquatabad after leaving work around 5pm. Another commuter said an ambulance carrying his feverish mother was stuck for about two hours near Civic Centre while they were travelling to a doctor in Saddar.“We pay bills on time but still face 12-hour power outages. Today we couldn’t even reach home,” commuter Imran from Gharibabad said.KE, however, attributed the prolonged outages in some affected areas to electricity theft and unpaid bills. A company spokesperson said outstanding dues from defaulters in Bandhani Colony and Rexer Line had crossed PKR 3 billion, adding that the duration of load-shedding depended on “electricity theft and the level of losses in the area”.The protests come as Karachi continues to grapple with an electricity crisis that is also affecting water supply, businesses and daily life across densely populated neighbourhoods.
Article Summary: Demonstrations reported in Pak Colony, Liaquatabad, Gharibabad, Nishtar Road, Bhimpura and Ranchore Line. Protesters blocked major roads and intersections, burned tyres and clashed with K-Electric personnel. Residents said they were facing 12 hours or more of daily power cuts, often without adequate notice.

Article Title: 'India could use water as weapon': Pakistan minister as Indus Waters Treaty remains in abeyance
Article Text:
Pakistan minister Ahsan Iqbal (File photo)

Pakistan minister Ahsan Iqbal has said India could “weaponise” the Indus Water Treaty (IWT) and expressed hope that “better sense” would prevail to prevent the two neighbours from going to war again, this time over water.He noted that the treaty had remained “untouchable” for almost seven decades since it was signed in 1960, but New Delhi has now been kept in abeyance “unilaterally."“...Indus Water Treaty that has stood the test of time for the last 70 years. India and Pakistan fought several wars, but it (IWT) was considered untouchable because it is an international agreement, and this time around the Indian government has unilaterally held it in abeyance... first time probably water has been weaponised in history,” Iqbal told the Asia Society.“We (Pakistan) now face this threat that they (India) can use water as a weapon to deny Pakistan when it needs it for its crops and release it when we don't need it... We are using all the diplomatic means to make sure that we don't have future wars on water because we have already seen lots of wars,” the minister added.He further stated that South Asian countries should instead focus on issues such as development, poverty, illiteracy and the youth “bulge”, describing the region as the “least integrated” in the world."So we hope that there is better sense in our neighbour's (India) mind and we don't see that water is weaponised and we go to another conflict with India over water because Pakistan cannot surrender at any cost the future of its 250 million people for its food security and right of water. If we let it happen, then every state that is on the lower side of water supply would be hostage to any country that controls the rivers," the Pakistan Muslim League (Nawaz) leader remarked.Iqbal's remarks came days after Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif warned India of a “direct response” for putting the IWT in abeyance.“India proved itself an enemy of peace by unilaterally and illegally suspending the Indus Waters Treaty. I declare in clear terms that every single drop of Pakistan's water is our red line. If India does not come to its senses, it will be responded to directly,” Sharif said on August 13, on the eve of Pakistan's Independence Day.New Delhi put the agreement in abeyance following the Pahalgam terror attack in April last year. Since then, Pakistani leaders have repeatedly called water their “red line” and threatened India over the move, describing it as an “act of war.”
Article Summary: Ahsan Iqbal says India could use water as a weapon to deny Pakistan when it needs it for its crops. New Delhi put the agreement in abeyance following the Pahalgam terror attack in April last year. Pakistani leaders have repeatedly called water their “red line” and threatened India.

Article Title: ‘In contempt for gathering people’: Pak blames ex PM Imran Khan’s party for hospital transfer
Article Text:
Pakistan government statement on Imran Khan's hospital transfer

Poll Vote & Share your view How do you view the involvement of PTI workers during Imran Khan transfer to the hospital? Justified, they were supporting their leader Unsure 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Govt says court order was followed

NEW DELHI: The Pakistan government on Saturday blamed jailed former prime minister Imran Khan ’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party for his transfer to a state-run hospital instead of the private facility ordered by the Supreme Court for his medical checkup.Information minister Attaullah Tarar said the government was forced to take 73-year-old Khan to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) after a large number of PTI workers gathered outside Shifa International Hospital.The development came after Khan’s sister, Uzma Khan, approached the Supreme Court alleging that the government and senior officials had violated its order to shift the former prime minister to the private hospital.The Supreme Court had on August 18 directed authorities to transfer Khan from Adiala jail to Shifa Hospital within two days and keep him there until the next hearing on September 16. Instead, Khan was taken to PIMS and later returned to jail after doctors declared him fit.Tarar alleged that PTI workers gathered along the route to Shifa Hospital, removed barriers and created social media content, leaving authorities with no option but to shift Khan elsewhere.“Contempt has definitely happened,” Tarar said, accusing Khan’s sister and PTI of violating the court’s directions by turning the medical checkup into a political issue.The minister maintained that the government had implemented the Supreme Court’s order “in letter and spirit”. He said the medical examination was conducted transparently, Khan’s sister was present and doctors from Shifa Hospital were involved in the process.The Supreme Court’s order followed months of concerns raised by Khan’s family and supporters over his health, particularly an eye condition diagnosed earlier this year. Khan was taken to PIMS several times after being diagnosed with right central retinal vein occlusion in late January.A report submitted by jail authorities to the Supreme Court said his eye condition had improved significantly and that his vision was “almost normal”.Khan has been lodged in Rawalpindi’s Adiala Jail since 2023 in connection with several cases.
Article Summary: Pakistan government blames jailed former prime minister Imran Khan ’s Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party for his transfer to a state-run hospital. Information minister Attaullah Tarar said the government was forced to take 73-year-old Khan to the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences. Tarar alleged that PTI workers gathered along the route to Shifa Hospital, removed barriers and created social media content.

Article Title: Big crisis brewing in Rawalpindi? Pakistan deploys army for ‘sensitive duties’
Article Text:
The decision comes days after a man allegedly linked to former prime minister Imran Khan's party.

Army deployment follows security incident

Rawalpindi has strategic importance

The Pakistan government has authorised the deployment of the army in Rawalpindi for six months following a request from the Punjab home department for what it described as "sensitive security duties".The decision allows three companies of the Pakistan Army to be deployed in the city under Article 245 of the Pakistani Constitution, which permits the armed forces to assist the civil administration in maintaining security."The federal government, exercising the powers conferred under Article 245 of the Constitution of Pakistan, is pleased to authorise the deployment of three companies of the Pakistan Army for sensitive security duties in Rawalpindi," according to a notification issued by the Ministry of Interior and Narcotics Control on Friday.The notification said the deployment was intended to prevent a potential security problem and ensure that authorities could respond quickly if an unexpected situation arose.It said that the decision was taken "to avoid any undesirable situation as well as to respond effectively in any unforeseen situation as per the requirement of the district administration".The decision comes days after a man allegedly linked to former prime minister Imran Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf party opened fire at security forces in Rawalpindi.He was subsequently killed in retaliatory firing.State-run PTV News, citing security sources, reported that the attacker was a resident of Khyber district and an "active PTI member". According to the report, a PTI flag, bullets and weapons were recovered from him.The PTI, however, rejected any connection with the incident. The party said it had nothing to do with terrorism and accused authorities of attempting to associate the party with the attack.The deployment is particularly significant because Rawalpindi is home to the Pakistan Army's General Headquarters, the military's top command centre.The city is therefore an important military and administrative centre, and the decision to deploy army personnel there comes amid heightened security concerns following the recent shooting incident.The deployment has been authorised for six months, with the troops to perform duties requested by the district administration under the constitutional provision allowing the military to assist civilian authorities.
Article Summary: Three companies of the Pakistan Army will be deployed in Rawalpindi for six months. The decision comes after a man allegedly linked to Imran Khan's party opened fire in the city. The deployment is intended to prevent a potential security problem and ensure that authorities can respond quickly.

Article Title: 'Repeatedly tortured': Imran Khan's sister alleges abuse in jail as ex-Pakistan PM returns to prison
Article Text:
‘He was repeatedly tortured in jail’: Imran Khan's sister alleges mistreatment

PTI files contempt petition

Supporters gather after brief hospital visit

Pakistan's jailed former Prime Minister Imran Khan repeatedly told his sister that he was being tortured in prison, she said on Saturday, a day after he was taken to a state-run hospital for a brief medical examination and sent back to jail.Khan's sister, Uzma Khan, attended his examination at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences (PIMS) in Islamabad and said the former prime minister was physically fit but had repeatedly complained of torture.“Khan told me that he is being repeatedly tortured in prison”, she told the media.The interior and law ministries, along with jail authorities, have not responded to a Reuters request for comment on the allegation.Khan was taken to PIMS overnight on Friday after the Supreme Court had directed authorities to transfer him from Adiala jail to Shifa International Hospital in Islamabad for a medical examination. He was declared medically fit and returned to prison within hours.Khan's Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf (PTI) party on Saturday filed a contempt petition against the government, accusing authorities of violating the Supreme Court's order by taking him to PIMS instead of the private hospital named by the court.The petition seeks action against senior government officials and asks that Khan be taken to Shifa International Hospital for treatment, PTI legal adviser Naeem Panjutha said."The petition seeks action against the ​prime minister, law minister, information minister" and other government officials, Panjutha said, adding that it also calls for Khan's treatment at the private hospital ordered by the court.The PTI also alleged that Khan was denied access to his personal physician, which it said amounted to another breach of the Supreme Court's directive.A three-judge Supreme Court bench had on Tuesday directed authorities to transfer Khan from Adiala jail to Shifa International Hospital within two days for a medical examination.The PTI interprets the order as requiring Khan to remain under medical supervision until at least mid-September.Information Minister Attaullah Tarar said the decision to take Khan to PIMS instead of the court-named private hospital was made because of security concerns.Khan declared medically fit, sent back to jailKhan was examined by a team of doctors, including an ophthalmologist, cardiologist and physician, before being declared medically fit and sent back to Adiala jail in Rawalpindi."A team of qualified doctors, including an ophthalmologist, a cardiologist and a physician conducted a detailed examination of him and declared him medically fit," Tarar said.Khan has been imprisoned since August 2023 and maintains that the cases against him are politically motivated. The government denies the allegation.His lawyers have previously said his health has deteriorated in prison and that he has suffered substantial loss of vision in his right eye. Article Title: Ex-Pak PM Imran Khan moved to private hospital from prison after SC order
